reviews.comment: He is an alright lecturer. He can be a bit cringey though, like during our class he was obsessed with 67. The homework is BY FAR the most time consuming part of the class so start it early.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He gave great in depth lectures, and I was able to exclusively use his slides to study for exams. The exams are not too bad if you took a CS class before. Since the course was common, the homework was the same for each professor. Each homework took a very long time. He cares for his students success and was approachable in and out of class.

Beideman was a decent prof, though towards the end he lost my attention since his class got a bit boring. Exams are not too bad since you get to bring 5 front/back pages worth of cheat sheet. However, (this is for all profs anyway) START THE HOMEWORK EARLY!! The homework is the most tedious part of the class BY FAR and WILL take hours!!!

ignore the other reviews about bad handwriting he revised all his slides with typed-out stuff and beautiful diagrams. exams were 75% of our grade which is quite a bit but i found the rpactice exams were decent material to prepare for em. Lectures are not too bad to follow and definitely better than the textbook. grading is not too harsh.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is exam heavy and has mandatory attendance, but unfortunately does it at the end of the class. He considers almost anything ch3ating, and I believe he "caught" 60+ people in my semester. The class isn't difficult, ESPECIALLY if you already come from a coding background.
Solid lectures with good explanations. Class is exam heavy but they are pretty easy. Professor is always willing to answer questions.

the weekly homeworks are hard but very helpful in teaching. Not a fan of his lecture style, often fell asleep or got distracted, but im a very easily distracted person so I can't  give a fair rating on that. Exams are easy if you do your homework and actually practice beforehand. There are also many C++ resources online that helped me.

He's one of the better professors for 120. His lectures are generally more in-depth, making certain things easier to understand. The course is standardized tho, so prof doesn't really matter that much. Exam code tracing is very similar to the practice material, and if you understand how to do the labs/homeworks yourself, frq should be a breeze

Homeworks take forever, but are really beneficial for learning the content. In depth and clear lectures, so even just paying attention will serve you really well. We were allowed 5 cheat sheets front and back for each exam, and each exam lined up well with class content.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Fair course all around and he was a really nice guy, lectures were clear and well structured. I enjoyed attending his class.

Probably the most in-depth lectures you'll get for 120. I have friends with other professors who use his slides to study for exams. Just pay attention in lecture and you'll be fine, but you should also be able to use what you learn from the homeworks to get caught up. He does non-graded pop quizzes every class which are good to refresh things.

Homework was by far the most challenging part of this course, but there were unlimited submissions. On average I spent like 2-5 hours each week. Lectures were pretty fast and unengaging so I stopped taking notes. The exams are fairly easy and make up a large portion of the final grade.

This was his first time teaching 221, so his test difficulty and preparedness may not have been perfectly calibrated. Overall, I thought his lecture slides were very thorough (even if the actual lecture was hard to follow), and exams matched up with his reviews. 2 pages of cheat sheets allowed on every exam were very helpful.

He's OK. He lectures faster than the speed of light and I gave up taking notes halfway through. Homework takes quite a bit of time but doable if you manage. Get some cushion with the first two exams because they are the easiest.

The professor was disorganized during lectures but his lecture slides were in depth to grasp the theory. He also had exam reviews with MCQ and short answer that reflected the actual exams and challenging code-writing questions to help prepare for the exam. His exams are not bad if you take your time to study the material.

I took him for both 120 and 221. He writes his own 221 exams, and they're very difficult, but you get cheat sheets (unlike other profs!). It was his first time teaching 221, so a bit rusty at first, but he improved a lot. His exam reviews got better and more detailed. I think his next 221 semester will be smoother now that expectations are clearer.
Totally disregard his good ratings when it comes to the 221 and 411 classes. Good for beginning classes, bad for intermediate/advanced CS classes. Lectures are okay, but exams are BAD.

Attendance and lab are mandatory and big parts of the grade. The homework is tough, though it has unlimited resubmissions. Exams are reasonable. It's an easy class and a guaranteed B if you do the work and show up. I did poorly all semester but did well on the final and used the final + midterm replacement to save my grade. Very generous grading.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Read off lecture slides but the slides themselves were pretty helpful. Also had really useful code examples that come in handy during labs, homework, and exams. Chill guy but this is also an easy class.

Pains me to write this because the guy is super chill, but such a bad prof for this class. Exams are insane compared to other profs, very disorganized lectures, and some of the TAs are just awful. I should have just taken Leyk.
HIS EXAMS ARE INSANE COMPARED TO THE OTHER PROFFESSORS IF I FAILLL THIS CLASS IM SUING. !!!!!!! . Also he doesn't respond to emails like at all just take another prof :<
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I think this was his first time teaching 221... His exams are terrible compared to Leyk's and his lectures are often useless. If you end up with him youtube will be your best friend. He seems to care about the content, just has trouble teaching. He is also not a rude person by any means, just doesn't have the experience teaching I guess.

Most disorganized professor encountered so far. Shows up late to every lecture, drones through the lecture slides (with plenty of mistakes in them), unreadable handwriting, and his tests are just straight up not fair compared to other professors. Very difficult to talk to him 1 on 1 and never responds to emails. Take someone else, TA are lifesavers
beideman type stuff

It's hard to stay focused in his lectures, he mostly just rambles and reads off slides. He does do examples by hand which is helpful at times. The exams are very difficult and the TA I had was an insanely tough grader so not all the slack falls on him. This class is also hard in general, I'd take someone else.

He was a great lecturer and explained everything well. He also answered all of my questions, even though I had a lot of them. The exams were also really simple and were far easier than questions given to you on leetcode. Overall a great professor and a relatively easy class.

His lectures were good at explaining the material tested on the homework and exams. Your grade is mostly dependent on homework and exams, which are common for all CSCE 120 sections. Homework can get very tedious, so make sure you don't procrastinate on them. You get to have cheat sheets for the exams, which are very helpful.

Dr. Beideman knows what he is doing very well, and is great at explaining stuff. However, because he is so intelligent, if you ask a dumb question, he will make you look stupid, especially in front of the whole class. I liked him a lot, has a unique sense of humor and very good teacher. Pretty enjoyable class overall.

One of the best lecturers for 120, however the coursework for all profs is the same (except attendance). Just show up to 36/42 lectures for full credit for him. Start on HWs early and utilize all resources (TA/prof office hours). Get a 100 for all averages (very possible) and you only need 75 exam average for an A. Cheat sheets for exams allowed.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty much all of CSCE 120 is the same, so it doesn't matter which professor you take. Dr. Beideman was great, but I felt his lectures tended to drone on just a little bit. Would still take his class again though.

While a lot of the material you learn is from Zybook, online resources, and always going to office hours, Beideman is still a good prof at covering his slides and in-class examples. He always takes time after class to help the line of students having questions over the homework (not his fault though; The homework is just a LOT). I'd recommend him.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Great choice for CSCE 120. He placed tricky code problems at the end of lectures, which helped a lot for the exams(participation based). He explained the more difficult topics well and was easy to follow.If you need more help go to his OH or the TA's OH. There's also a 120 discord for this class which helped a lot. Overall, great choice.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: He's a great professor, clear lectures with great examples that make you think and understand basic concepts. He has a daily attendance quiz (participation grade) and you also have a couple skip so you can skip a couple days and still get full credit. Tests were a little tuff but you get 5 pages of cheat sheets. He's a little bit of a pushover.

Dr. Beideman was a very kind and caring professor who attempted to help students in a more demanding CSCE class as best he could. There was partial credit on the exams and homework, and although the lectures were the basic concepts, the exams were quite similar to the homework which was enough to get a good chunk of points.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty good, easy to understand and follow. Gives a "quiz" at the end of class which is very confusing but helped prepare for tests as they were similar and were only for attendance (participation credit). The hw was tough for this class in general towards the end, however help is easily available through the discord server and TAs
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof Beideman is a pleasant guy but has very hard to follow lectures, partly because most of the slide content is scribbled during class. The tests are difficult but manageable. The homeworks are harshly graded to a very specific rubric, so if you use a slightly out of the box algo then each week you have to go to the TA to argue for points back.

Gave boring and jargon-heavy lectures which were hard to follow and stay engaged. Little to no interactions with students during lecture. Lectures did not prepare me well for homework and exams so I had to use YouTube and other outside resources to study. A nice guy but I would recommend taking other professors for 411.

I didn't have any prior coding experience, so I did struggle with this class a bit. However, his lectures were always clear, and much of the learning came from the zyBooks too. He is a bit of a pushover in the way that the lectures were never quiet; the students would talk over him so much.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: His 120 class seems a lot better than this one, homeworks are unbelievably hard even when working in a group of 4. This guy is too smart to teach, really bad handwriting and also doesn't explain complicated stuff digestibly. Exams are loads easier than the homeworks but we do not get a good foundation in lecture, so lots of Q drops.

The CSCE 120 reviews do not apply to this course at all. He just scribbles on the board and expects us to have the same level of understanding he does. He will fail you and not give you a curve despite how ill-prepared you are. And the homework is ridiculous. This review sounds harsh, but he is ten times harsher on us than we could ever be on him.

I had to q-drop this class. The homeworks were brutal. You're allowed to work in a group of 4 for a 4-question HW each week and it was still taking us ~5 hours each and our grades were always in the 60s-70s. The one exam I took was also hard. The lectures just don't prepare you for the questions you're asked on HWs or exams. Lecture felt pointless.

Beidemann is a great professor. The majority of the course is lab assignments/homework/zybooks/participation, but his lectures are great for learning new concepts and visualizing them. Exams were generous with partial credit and he reviewed prior to them. Homework takes a long time, so working ahead is ideal.
Professor Beideman is new to teaching, but he is very fair and caring of his students. Lectures can be a little boring, but I think that will be fixed as he gets more teaching experience.

Great lectures, explained everything thoroughly. If a question was asked about something he didn't know, he would test it out during class. Exams were reasonable and actually good tests of your knowledge of C++ and problem solving skills. Attendance taken each class for participation grade, about 1 week given for each homework.

I think he was a TA at Carnegie & UIUC so he teaches/explains really well. His lecture slides are AMAZING on god. I used his lecture slides to study for my exams, labs, and do homework. Plus, he updates them in the drive w/ practice code. Generally, the directions on the homeworks are garbage but referring to his notes made life easier.

120 is very homework and test-oriented, but his lectures explain the content covered in both very well. He provides thorough slides and works through examples, as well as provides a day dedicated to reviewing topics for exams. He's very helpful and easy to talk to, both in and out of class.
He is very thorough in his lectures and cares for his students. Almost any question I had would get answered in the lecture without me even asking. Would totally recommend. Do the homework on time.

Dr. Beideman is an incredible lecturer, especially considering it's his first semester of teaching. His slides are extremely thorough and he gives concrete examples for every topic discussed in class. His office hours are WAY more helpful than the PT-central office hours, and it's clear he puts effort in to make sure his students succeed. Take him!

He was able to explain everything clearly and concisely, with very good power point slides to drive the topic home. He does have quizzes every lecture to take attendance, most of which are trick questions, but they are only a participation grade and does a good job of explaining the correct answer afterwards. Very good professor overall.

Beideman is a great lecturer and responds well to questions during class. CSCE 120's work load can be heavy, but as long as you stay on top of things this class is an easy A. Beideman has mandatory attendance quizzes that are participation-based that can be quite tricky, but are a great way to learn the fundamentals of C++.
reviews.ratingTags: Amazing lectures --Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He's fairly nice and does his best to explain the relevant concepts. Lectures aren't always the most engaging but they're posted on Canvas anyways so you can review them as needed and he's responsive to questions in class. Show up to class for the attendance quizzes, but overall just stay on top of your homework and you should be fine
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes
